result.Method of Attack: Continuously scans random IPv4 addresses for exposed SSH services on TCP port 22, attempts authentication using a local username-password wordlist, disables SSH host key verification, and on first successful login exfiltrates credentials (IP, username, password) to a hardcoded Telegram bot controlled by the threat actor, then exits.
Impacted Systems: Hastily provisioned Linux hosts with default credentials
Attack Vector: Running the malicious Go package by operators
Scanning and brute forcing SSH services on random IPv4 addresses
Exfiltration via Telegram Bot API over HTTPS
Indicators of Compromise: Telegram Bot name and handle: ssh_bot (@sshZXC_bot)
Embedded SSH brute force wordlist (wl.txt) pairing root and admin with weak/default passwords such as toor, raspberry, dietpi, alpine, password, qwerty, 123456, webadmin, webmaster
Use of ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey() to skip host verification
Code functions: IsOpened (port scanning), ssh.ClientConfig with ssh.Password authentication, http.Get to Telegram API
